PRD, capability status and technical truth

A source-linked technical walkthrough. Trace the flow, explain the boundary, then test the failure path.

After this session, you can:
  • Use the canonical product definition
  • Distinguish implemented from production-ready
  • Find evidence for a capability claim

Technical flow

Every hand-off is a control boundary: on failure the flow holds, refers or denies — it never skips ahead.

  1. 01Product definition
  2. 02Capability catalogue
  3. 03Architecture contract
  4. 04Code + tests
  5. 05Trace evidence
  6. 06Tenant production admission

1. The PRD stack

The canonical product definition is what-we-are-building.md.

The complete-system capability catalogue decomposes that intent into stable capability IDs and maturity.

The journey support matrix owns public maturity for all 21 product journeys.

Architecture documents explain the designed boundary; current-implementation.md explains what exists.

2. Evidence beats page presence

A screen, lesson or route is not proof of production readiness.

Capability trace records connect a requirement to code, tests and documents.

Live providers, tenant configuration, UAT, security, DR and witnessed operating effectiveness may still be required.

3. Change discipline

When code and a load-bearing architecture source disagree, reconcile the design explicitly.

User-visible workflow changes update Guide/Academy content.

Structural decisions need ADRs; decision-engine changes must map to INV, DEC and SEC obligations.
